ref_extractions.title: Resting-State Theta and Alpha Oscillations in Amputation and Phantom Limb Pain: A Pre-Registered High-Density EEG Study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses the openneuro_ds006921 dataset (confirming 13 AmpPLP, 6 AmpNoPLP, 19 IC subjects) but performs traditional statistical analysis (mixed-effects models, bootstrap inference, cluster-based permutation) rather than ML classification. The analysis investigates group differences in theta power and peak alpha frequency as research questions, not as features for a predictive ML task. The paper defines group labels but does not construct an ML pipeline with those labels.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: 7-minute continuous recordings per condition (eyes-open, eyes-closed); multiple recordings per session; no epoch-level segmentation used
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: The analysis.md describes an ML classification task (epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5) but this paper does NOT implement it; it uses only statistical group comparison methods.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper explicitly references dataset from openneuro_ds006921, uses group labels (AmpPLP/AmpNoPLP/IC) derived from participants.tsv metadata, but applies mixed-effects models and permutation testing rather than ML classification. EEG collected with 64/128 electrodes (58 used in analysis), 7-minute recordings per condition.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has identifiable group labels (AmpPLP/AmpNoPLP/IC) and clear paradigm structure for resting-state group classification. However, the only 'partial' reference (paper_10_21203_rs_3_rs_8645281_v1.pdf) explicitly states 'supports_task: false' and uses mixed-effects models rather than ML classification, while the other two references are classified as 'uncertain'. The analysis.md provides task definitions, but without at least one reference that supports ML classification, feasibility cannot be established.
